items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-08-01
items.q: Well Raymond was playing with us at that time.

ctx.x: Well you had Kappa, you were out on that label Kappa. Yeah. Yeah, I remember you played Tin Roof. Raymond. Oh yeah, that's a good shot of Raymond. I was waiting for that.
Well Raymond was playing with us at that time. Yeah. When, when, there's my leg there. Uh huh. When, when Lester Bouchon got so ill. Yeah.

Had to have those operations. That's Raymond Burke. Yes. Uh huh. You know Raymond had to get all the zippers taken off of his pants. Huh? He wiggled so much. He had to have all the zippers taken off of his pants. And buttons put on them. He wiggled so much. Oh no. He wiggled so much. He wiggled so much. Oh no. He wiggled so much. Oh no. And he played that his zipper would come out and sell time. He would gradually work itself down to where the fly was open.

items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-07-14
items.q: Raymond and I first met at the Edgewater Gulf

ctx.x: He's too shy to make a phone call. He played with his brother. I was talking about when I was so nervous before getting married, I didn't know what to do. I couldn't find anybody to talk to, so I called up his brother, and we talked about Raymond. Raymond played over there, I guess in Faro with him.

Oh, yes. Raymond and I first met at the Edgewater Gulf, and Raymond was playing at the Midway Inn, and I was playing with Johnny Batusi, Toots Batusi, the old man, at the Midway at another time, and Raymond came over and played some spot jobs at the Edgewater Gulf with some fiddle player. I don't quite remember his name.
I'll have to ask Raymond about that.
